lesson.title: Reaction Time Kinematics Lab
lesson.buzzAssessmentTitle: Unit 1 Lesson 4: Reaction Time Kinematics Lab

gradingDesign.rule: All variable student evidence is graded only in the final two BusyBee responses.

questions.prompt: In Level 1, the ruler starts at rest and falls under gravity during your reaction time. Which equation models how far it falls?
A ruler falls 19.6 cm before it is caught. What is the reaction time in seconds?
Approximately how far would the ruler fall during a 0.100 s reaction time? Enter the distance in centimeters.
A dragster accelerates from rest at 40 m/s^2 down the 300 m strip. How many seconds of driving does it take to reach the finish line, excluding reaction time?
You react in 0.400 s and the computer reacts in 0.250 s. Both dragsters then accelerate at 40 m/s^2. What is the gap in meters when the leading car crosses the 300 m finish line?
In Level 3, both sprinters run at a steady 10 m/s. Which equation gives distance traveled after the runner starts?
Both sprinters run at 10.0 m/s. The opponent reacts in 0.150 s and you react in 0.300 s. By how many meters does the opponent lead at the finish?
Why does a start faster than 0.100 s count as a false start in the sprint level?

Compare one visual reaction-time result from Level 1 or 2 with one auditory reaction-time result from Level 3. Cite both values, calculate or estimate their difference, and state which signal produced your faster response.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Use one visual and one auditory value from your own trials and make a conclusion consistent with them.
a. Full credit: Cites both reaction times with units, gives a reasonable difference, identifies the faster response, and makes a conclusion supported by the values.
  Partial credit: Gives values for both signal types but omits the difference or conclusion, or provides a correct comparison with only one clearly cited value.
  No credit: Cites no usable trial values, compares unlike quantities, or states a conclusion that contradicts the evidence.

questions.prompt: Use one Level 2 drag race and one Level 3 sprint to explain how a reaction-time head start affects the finish gap differently during accelerated motion and constant-speed motion. Cite reaction times or gaps from both trials.
questions.rubricText:
@[Always] Compare the motion models, use evidence from both levels, and explain why the accelerating gap grows while the constant-speed gap stays fixed after both runners begin.
a. Full credit: Cites evidence from both levels, explains that the earlier dragster is always farther along its acceleration history and therefore faster at the same clock time, explains that equal constant sprint speeds preserve the reaction-time distance lead, and connects both effects to the finish gaps.
  Partial credit: Correctly contrasts the two gaps but omits evidence from one level or gives an incomplete explanation of the acceleration case.
  No credit: Attributes the Level 2 result to different accelerations, says the constant-speed gap keeps growing after both start, or provides no trial evidence.
